costGuide.title: Suzuki K15C Engine Replacement Cost (UK)
costGuide.labourLine: Fitting a K15C typically takes 8-11 hours at £65-£75/hr (independent) - confirm exact labour when comparing quotes. Hybrid system integration adds complexity compared to non-hybrid Suzuki petrol engines.
paragraphs: The K15C's hybrid system adds complexity to replacement - the 140V lithium-ion battery, Integrated Starter Generator (ISG), and inverter must be properly integrated with the replacement unit. A unit with a documented hybrid system health check will command a premium. The AGS gearbox (automated manual) is a separate component but should be inspected when replacing the engine. See our full reconditioned engine cost guide for detailed breakdowns.

failures.title: Suzuki K15C Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Hybrid System Sensor and Control Module Issues - 20,000-60,000 miles
items.whatHappens: The K15C's hybrid system - including the 140V lithium-ion battery, Integrated Starter Generator (ISG), and inverter - can suffer from sensor errors and control module glitches. These issues often manifest as warning lights, reduced hybrid assist, or the engine running more frequently than expected. Moisture ingress into connectors and weak 12V batteries are common triggers.
items.repairVsReplace: Most hybrid system issues are repairable through diagnostics, sensor replacement, or software updates (£200-£800). However, if the hybrid battery or inverter fails, replacement costs can be significant - the lithium-ion battery alone can cost £1,500-£3,000 to replace. Read our full hybrid system failure guide .

items.title: AGS Gearbox Behaviour - All mileages
items.onset: From new - characteristic rather than failure
items.whatHappens: The K15C is paired with Suzuki's 6-speed AGS (Automated Gear Shift) robotised manual gearbox. This is not a conventional automatic - it operates like a manual gearbox with an automated clutch. The system is known for jerky engagement, especially when cold, and slow, hesitant shifts. While this is a design characteristic rather than a mechanical failure, it is the most common owner complaint and can feel like a fault.
items.repairVsReplace: The AGS behaviour is typically not a failure - it's a characteristic of the system. However, clutch wear can occur in heavy urban use, with clutch replacement costing £600-£1,200. A modified driving style - lifting off the accelerator slightly before expected gear changes - improves smoothness significantly.

items.title: Timing Chain Wear - 80,000-150,000 miles (potential)
items.whatHappens: The K15C uses a maintenance-free timing chain rather than a belt. However, some reports suggest potential for early timing chain wear or stretching in certain conditions. Symptoms include rattling noises from the engine when cold or at specific RPM ranges. The engine is sensitive to oil viscosity - using incorrect or thick oil can accelerate VVT system wear.
items.repairVsReplace: If caught early, timing chain and tensioner replacement costs £600-£1,200. If the chain skips or snaps, full engine replacement is the only option.

failures.goodYearsLine: The K15C is a relatively new engine, and systematic problems are not yet well-documented. Hybrid system issues appear more common on 2022-2023 production, with later units showing improvement. The engine itself is considered fundamentally sound.

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the Suzuki K15C
variants.intro: The K15C is the latest evolution of Suzuki's 1.5-litre K-series petrol engine, distinguished from its predecessor the K15B by the addition of full hybrid (FHEV) technology, DualJet injection (two injectors per cylinder), and a 140V electrical system. It is a naturally aspirated, all-aluminium engine with a maintenance-free timing chain. Where to find your engine code: The engine code is stamped on a metal plate on the cylinder block, visible from the top of the engine bay. The engine number on the V5C starts with K15C followed by seven digits. Alternatively, check the vehicle identification plate or use the registration lookup above. Commonly confused codes: - K15B - The earlier 1.5 DualJet engine without full hybrid. It has a similar block but lacks the 140V hybrid system, ISG motor, and some DualJet injection components. Not a direct swap - the K15C's hybrid system requires specific wiring and ECU integration. - K14C - The 1.4-litre Boosterjet turbo petrol, a completely different engine family. Not compatible. Why getting the right code matters: The K15C's full hybrid system is integral to the engine's operation - fitting a non-hybrid K15B or a K14C turbo engine would require extensive rewiring, ECU replacement, and hybrid system removal or adaptation. Always match the engine code exactly when buying a replacement.

relatives.description: : The K15B was the previous generation 1.5-litre DualJet engine, fitted to Vitara and S-Cross models from 2015-2022. It shares the same basic block and DualJet injection system but lacks the K15C's 140V full hybrid system, Integrated Starter Generator (ISG), and the revised combustion chamber design. The K15B is a simpler engine - cheaper to replace but less fuel-efficient.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement Suzuki K15C - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: ** A used K15C makes sense for lower-value Vitara or S-Cross examples where the cost of a reconditioned unit would be disproportionate. Used units from £800-£1,500 are available from Suzuki breakers. However, a used K15C only makes sense with documented hybrid system health - the 140V battery and ISG motor are expensive to replace separately. Without a full hybrid system check, budget £1,500-£3,000 for potential hybrid component replacement. Link: used engines

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: ** A proper K15C recon (£1,800-£2,800) addresses the specific complexities of this hybrid engine - full hybrid system health check, new timing chain and tensioner, rebuilt cylinder head, and a full inspection of the ISG motor and inverter. For most Vitara and S-Cross owners, this is the sweet spot - reliable, warrantied, and well within the vehicle's value on most examples. Link: reconditioned engines

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: ** A full K15C rebuild (£2,800-£4,200) is justified for low-mileage, well-maintained examples where the owner wants to preserve the vehicle. An upgraded rebuild should include a new hybrid battery (if degraded), new injectors, a fully overhauled cylinder head, and a new timing chain kit. Link: rebuilt engines

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: ** All our vetted UK Suzuki hybrid specialists offer supply-only or full supply-and-fit on K15C units - fitted prices include 8-11 hours of labour, specialist hybrid system fluids, and a 12-24 month warranty. Nationwide delivery covers supply-only orders. Link: supply and fit
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: ** The K15C sits in host vehicles with UK market values ranging from £8,000 (early high-mileage Vitara) to £25,000 (late low-mileage S-Cross) . If your K15C host is worth less than £10,000, a reconditioned K15C at £1,800-£2,800 will represent 18-35% of the vehicle's value - a viable proposition. For hosts above £15,000, the reconditioned unit is a clear investment, adding several years of life to a car worth keeping.

items.question: Which Suzuki models use the K15C engine?
items.answer: The K15C powers the Suzuki Vitara (IV generation, 2022-present facelift) and the Suzuki SX4 S-Cross (III generation, 2022-present), both wearing 1.5 Dualjet Hybrid badges. It was introduced in the UK in 2022 as the full hybrid (FHEV) version of Suzuki's compact SUVs. items.question: How many miles can a Suzuki K15C engine last?
items.answer: The K15C is a new engine, so long‑term data is limited. With proper maintenance - including 10,000‑mile oil changes using the correct 0W‑20 oil - the combustion engine itself should exceed 150,000-200,000 miles. The hybrid system is the main variable; the 140V lithium‑ion battery is expected to last 8-10 years or 100,000-150,000 miles, depending on usage patterns. Strict oil spec (0W‑20) is essential for VVT system health; hybrid battery replacement costs £1,500-£3,000 when eventually needed; AGS clutch wear in urban use is a consideration.
